Title: Document 10
Content: Source: Vilma Espín, female scientist, president of the Federation of Cuban Women, and longtime member of the Cuban Communist Party's Central Committee, speech, `text(1989)`.

Women have successfully burst into the economic life of our country. At present, `39` `text(percent)` of the total labor force in the civil state economy is female, compared to `25` `text(percent)` in `text(1974)`, and in Havana, the figure is `45` `text(percent)`.

However, we have not yet seen the same progress on men's participation in the sphere of family life, in the fulfillment of their responsibilities as fathers and co-participants in the family. Spouses with the same degree of work commitments do not yet shoulder an equal burden.

Working women still bear the full responsibility for the education and formation of their children, as well as household organization and chores. This gives rise to the extremely unfair “`text(double)` work shift” that exhausts women.
